scope: Staging JSON checkpoint reliability only; no source acquisition, model/feature/publication or database changes.

original_failure.operation: Path.replace temporary complete JSON over existing progress.json
original_failure.observation: Temporary file was already flushed, fsynced and closed; the original implementation made one replacement attempt.

native_before_fix_reproduction.method: CreateFileW reader on the existing checkpoint; FILE_SHARE_READ|FILE_SHARE_WRITE without FILE_SHARE_DELETE
native_before_fix_reproduction.interpretation: Demonstrates the same OS failure mode; does not identify the process responsible for the original intermittent full-suite failure.

contracts: Brief native reader lock released during retry permits atomic commit.
Persistent native reader lock still fails after bounded attempts and preserves old complete JSON.
Synthetic Windows errors 5/32/33 recover transiently and propagate persistently.
Other permission errors and disk-full errors fail without retry or loss of old checkpoint.
Serialization and fsync failures never reach checkpoint replacement.
Successful first replacement has no retry delay.
The original checkpoint/resume staging regression and downloader suite pass.

references.title: Python 3.13 os.replace
references.relevance: Replacement can raise OSError; successful rename is the commit operation.

references.title: Microsoft CreateFileW file sharing
references.relevance: An open handle without FILE_SHARE_DELETE can prevent rename until it is closed.

references.title: Microsoft system error codes 0–499
references.relevance: Codes 5, 32 and 33 identify access-denied, sharing-violation and lock-violation failures.

limits: A short retry cannot cure permanent permissions or guarantee recovery from longer-lived locks.
The 150 ms bound is total requested sleep; operating-system I/O and scheduling time are separate.
No forecast scientific accuracy or full release-suite result is inferred from this focused reliability check.
